title: IntiCom-DB v2.0: An expanded manually curated resource for inter-tissue/organ communications
content:
by Qiong Zhou, Changxian Xiong, Linshu Wang, Huai Pang, Rucong Liu, Jingkun Yi, Yu Han, Yuan Zhou

Inter-tissue/organ communication (ITC) is essential for coordinating metabolism, immunity, development and disease progression. However, experimentally supported ITC events are dispersed across individual studies, hindering a systematic retrieval of their molecular mediators, source-to-target tissue routes and supporting evidence. Here, we present IntiCom-DB v2.0, an updated literature-derived database of experimentally supported ITC events. Compared with the previous version, IntiCom-DB v2.0 expands the curated collection to 1,862 entries from 1,485 publications, covering 651 unique ITC molecules across proteins, RNAs and metabolites. The updated database identifies 398 distinct communication routes between 51 source tissues and 53 target tissues, with protein-mediated events representing the largest category. To facilitate the functional interpretation of ITC-mediating proteins, IntiCom-DB v2.0 incorporates single-cell expression patterns, secretion-related features, post-translational modification sites and proteolytic processing information. The redesigned web interface supports the searching, browsing and visualization of ITC molecules and source-to-target routes, enabling users to explore tissue communication patterns and prioritize ITC mediators in complex diseases. Overall, IntiCom-DB v2.0 provides an expanded, standardized and functionally annotated resource for investigating long-range communications among various tissues and organs. IntiCom-DB v2.0 is freely available at http://rnanut.net/inticomdb.
author: Qiong Zhou
